name: Colorado
metaDescription: Check Colorado hunting season dates for 2026–27, including deer, elk, turkey and waterfowl, plus license steps and deadlines linked to CPW sources.
homepageSummary: CPW dates, draw steps and area-specific rules for Colorado hunting.
intro: Colorado’s 2026 seasons are organized around GMUs, hunt codes, license types and waterfowl zones—not one statewide opening date. Use this guide to find the statewide framework, then confirm the exact hunt code and current CPW rules before you go.
zoneNote: Big-game hunt codes and GMUs, turkey areas split by I-25 and GMU 140, and Central/Pacific Flyway waterfowl zones can change dates and eligibility. The published regulation and your license’s exact hunt code control.

licenseAndEducation.fact: Anyone born on or after Jan. 1, 1949 must complete an approved hunter-education course before applying for or buying a Colorado hunting license. Carry the card unless CPW has verified it and the license is marked V.

Applicants need valid identification, an SSN or ITIN if age 12+, hunter education, a qualifying license before applying, and a habitat stamp for ages 18–64. A qualifying license and application can be completed in one transaction if the qualifying license is added first.
Buy online through CPWShop, by phone at 1-800-244-5613, or in person at CPW offices, state parks and authorized sales agents. The CPWShop site includes a sales-agent locator.

Confirmed 2026 fees include a $12.76 habitat stamp ($384.16 lifetime). Turkey fees: resident processing $8.93, adult spring $38.49, fall $32.11, youth $20.62; nonresident processing $11.49, adult spring/fall $194.21, youth $130.39. Included fees may include search-and-rescue and Wildlife Management Fund charges.

Waterfowl hunters need a small-game license; hunters age 16+ also need the Colorado waterfowl stamp and federal migratory-bird stamp. Small-game, coyote and migratory-bird hunters must register with HIP before hunting.

Youth big-game hunting is generally ages 12–17, with a narrow exception for an 11-year-old who turns 12 before season end. Youth turkey licenses are reduced-cost; hunters under 16 must hunt turkey with an 18+ qualified mentor. Small-game license holders age 17 and younger require a mentor and hunter education.

Exact GMU-by-GMU dates, quotas, sex/antler restrictions, OTC versus limited status, private-land-only restrictions and special hunt-code dates cannot be exhaustively represented in this statewide summary; the official brochure and physical license control.
Live remaining-license inventory is dynamic and was not asserted; check CPWShop immediately before purchase.

The complete small-game brochure has additional species and zone/bag-limit tables, including grouse, ptarmigan, crane, sage-grouse, snipe, rail and furbearers; consult the full official PDF for those details.

Bighorn sheep and mountain goat unit/method dates in this guide: Not yet published - check Colorado Parks and Wildlife. The agency’s published 2026 Big Game brochure is the source for exact hunt-code calendars; these were not confirmed for this summary.
